lead.headline: US Employers Add 165,000 Jobs, but Pay Still Trails Prices
lead.deck: October hiring was far stronger than experts expected, yet wages are not rising as fast as the cost of living.
body: On Friday the Labor Department said US employers added 165,000 jobs in October. Unemployment, the share of people who want work but cannot find it, eased to 4.1 percent. AFP reported that experts had expected only 65,000 new jobs.
Hospitals, factories and transportation companies hired more people, while restaurants and construction companies let workers go. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1 percent over the past year.
Prices rose faster. Inflation, the rise in prices over time, reached 3.7 percent in September. So most workers can buy a little less than before.
The Federal Reserve, the US central bank, raised its main interest rate in September. Its next decision is on December 8-9.

map.caption: The jobs report covers workers across the whole United States.

lead.why: Jobs, pay and prices decide how far a family's money goes each week, and they guide the Federal Reserve when it sets interest rates, which affect loans.

world.kicker: WORLD  •  IRAN AND THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ
world.headline: Mediators Work to Stop US-Iran Fighting as Ships Are Hit
world.deck: Qatar and others urge a deal, while ships near a key oil route came under attack this week.
body: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow stretch of sea next to Iran. Oil and gas tankers sail through it, so trouble there can raise fuel prices far away. The United States and Israel began a war on Iran on February 28, and Iran effectively shut the strait early on.

This week the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said at least 11 ships were attacked in and around the strait, and three sank. On Friday night two projectiles hit Iran's Qeshm island; President Trump called them 'minor strikes'.
Talking goes on. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, spoke with 12 foreign ministers in 48 hours. Qatar's prime minister said the two sides should not wait for a 'perfect moment' to make a deal.

world.connect: Geography: the strait is a chokepoint, a narrow passage that many ships must use. Economics: when fewer tankers can pass, oil is harder to deliver, which can push fuel prices up around the world.

us.headline: Trump Picks Stephen Miller as His New Chief of Staff
us.deck: The president named his closest aide to run the White House team days after Republicans lost Congress.
body: A chief of staff manages a president's team of advisers. On Friday, November 6, President Trump announced that Stephen Miller will take the job 'starting Monday, November 9, 2026'.

Miller is 41. He is now the White House deputy chief of staff for policy and also the homeland security adviser, and he has been one of Trump's closest aides for more than a decade. He drove the government's mass deportation programme. He replaces Susie Wiles, the first woman in the job, whose last day was Friday.

The change follows the midterms, in which Republicans lost both the House and the Senate. Vice President Vance said the party lost because of the Iran war, and Trump said that was 'largely true'. Democrats take control of Congress in early January. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer vowed to oppose Miller's appointment.
us.why: The chief of staff shapes which plans move forward, so this choice hints at how Trump will work with Congress.
also: Democrats take control of Congress in early January.
Mike Johnson plans to step down as top House Republican, a source says.

india.headline: Odisha Asks for Rs 2,526 Crore After Cyclone and Floods
india.deck: Two cyclones in a week left roads, homes and jobs damaged along India's east coast.
body: A cyclone is a huge spinning storm. Two hit India's east coast in a week. Cyclone Murasu came ashore near Ongole, in Andhra Pradesh, at about 1:00 a.m. on Tuesday, November 3, after Cyclone Arnab brought floods to Odisha.

Before Murasu, officials planned to move about 30,000 people to safety. No deaths or injuries had been reported at that time. The storm still uprooted trees and power poles, wrecked fishing boats and hit crops in Prakasam and Bapatla districts.

In Odisha's Ganjam district, all the blocks, the small local areas, were affected, with roads cut off and houses damaged. The Odisha government sent the central government a memorandum, a formal written request, asking for Rs 2,526 crore for relief and rebuilding in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal. An eight-member central team has visited the damaged areas. The state's Congress chief, Bhakta Charan Das, wants Rs 5,000 crore and a national calamity declaration for the floods.
india.why: After a storm, families need roads, homes and work restored, and states often ask the national government for money to pay for it.

lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to The Breakfast Table for November 8. Today we look at jobs and prices, a busy sea route, and a new job at the White House.
Let's start with jobs. What happened?

On Friday the Labor Department said US employers added 165,000 jobs in October. Experts had expected far fewer, about 65,000. Unemployment, the share of people looking for work who cannot find it, eased to 4.1 percent.
So that sounds like good news for families.

Partly. Hospitals, factories and transportation companies hired more people. Restaurants and construction companies let workers go. And pay rose 3.1 percent over the past year, while prices rose faster. Inflation reached 3.7 percent in September. So most workers can buy a little less than before.
And that matters for interest rates too?
Yes. The Federal Reserve raised its main rate in September, and it decides again on December 8-9.
Next, the Strait of Hormuz. Where is it?

It is a narrow stretch of sea next to Iran. Oil and gas tankers sail through it, so trouble there can change fuel prices far away. The United States and Israel began a war on Iran on February 28, and Iran effectively shut the strait early on.
What happened this week?
The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said at least 11 ships were attacked in and around the strait in the week ending November 6, and three sank.
Is anyone trying to calm things down?
Yes. Qatar and other mediators keep talking to both sides. Qatar's prime minister said they should not wait for a perfect moment to make a deal.
Now to Washington. Who is Stephen Miller?
A chief of staff manages the president's team and helps run the White House day to day. President Trump named Stephen Miller, who is 41, to take the job starting Monday, November 9.
Who had the job before?

Susie Wiles, the first woman to hold it. Friday was her last day. The change comes after Republicans lost both the House and the Senate in the midterms, and Democrats take over Congress in early January.
And what do the Democrats say?

Vice President Vance said the party lost because of the Iran war, and Trump said that was 'largely true'. Democrats take control of Congress in early January. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer vowed to oppose Miller's appointment.
